name: Persistent Systems Ltd
title: Persistent Systems Ltd - 533179 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Persistent is buying Nagarro for EUR1.27bn EV (9.12x EBITDA) on debt, plus a ~$125m annual net-new deal; no capacity or supply signal, so this is an M&A and deal-wins story, not a capital-cycle one.

summary.headline: Persistent to acquire Nagarro at EV €1.27bn (€81/share cash) and signed a ~$650M, 6.5-year net-new deal adding ~$125M annual value.
summary.overview: Management held a Sunday call (28 June 2026) announcing two items: a net-new strategic deal with an existing large US-headquartered customer worth roughly $125M annually and about $650M over 6.5 years, and a voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro at €81 per share in cash. The Nagarro offer implies an equity value of about €1bn and EV of €1.27bn, funded by a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, with a 50% plus one share minimum acceptance. Persistent has already secured 21% via a share purchase agreement, and management board members intend to tender about 13-14%. Closing is expected around Q4 CY2026 or early Q1 CY2027, subject to regulatory approvals. No Q1 FY27 financial results were discussed on this call.

financial_highlights.metric: Nagarro EBIT margin CY25 / Q1 CY26

financial_highlights.value: 140% to undisturbed close (25-26 June); 94% to 3-month VWAP

segments.name: Persistent (standalone)
segments.commentary: Five-year revenue CAGR of about 23.9%, with North America about 81%+ of revenue and Europe about 8-8.5%. Team of 27,500 across 21 countries.

segments.name: Nagarro (target)
segments.commentary: 5-year revenue CAGR of 18.4%, with about 35% of revenue from North America and about 18,500 staff (13,500 in India). Strengths cited in SAP, Siemens, OpenAI reseller and industrial/consumer verticals; management says constant-currency growth was over 5% recently.

segments.name: Combined group
segments.commentary: Pro forma about $2.9bn revenue, 46,000+ staff across 40+ countries; mix of North America 62%, Europe 22%, Rest of World 16%. Management targets European revenue of 15%+ and $5bn aspiration by FY31.

guidance_outlook: Leverage (net debt / combined EBITDA) at close expected at 1.9x-2.5x depending on acceptance, reducing to about 1x by FY2030.
Transaction expected to be cash EPS accretive and reported EPS accretive in Year 1 excluding one-time transaction expenses.
Goodwill vs other intangibles split about 70:30; intangibles amortised over 8 years.
Acquisition-related bridge interest at Euribor plus 175-250bps, roughly 4.1%-4.8% (4.1%-4.5% quoted in Q&A).
Revenue and cost synergies to be detailed only after regulatory approvals; management says margins will be maintained or improved.
New large deal is accretive to revenue and margin from Q2 onwards with no major ramp-up needed.

Public offer timeline: BaFin filing within 4 weeks, offer clearance in 10 working days to 2 weeks, 4-week acceptance period plus optional 2-week extension; Persistent AGM late July to seek shareholder approval. Squeeze-out possible over about 2 years; no domination agreement intended for 2 years.
capex_capacity: Transaction is fully debt-funded via a committed €1.4bn Barclays bridge facility, which also covers Nagarro refinancing if required, backed by a Persistent parent corporate guarantee.
Management said it does not intend a QIP or further dilution; private equity participation at asset level is being considered but no decision taken.
Management said it has moved from capex-heavy models to an opex model, funding working capital to support cash generation.
demand_pricing: Net new large deal from an existing US-headquartered technology customer: ~$125M annually and ~$650M+ over 6.5 years; customer name not disclosed under NDA.
Persistent has two $100M+ accounts, with a third approaching; the combined entity has 180 logos above $1M (Nagarro's largest customer under $50M) and over 350 $1M+ accounts.
Customer overlap between the two companies is in the single digits, with fewer than 10 significant overlapping customers.

Management said T&M model will decline over time but is not dead; Nagarro's T&M share was cited as 65-68% by analysts. Cannibalisation of T&M revenue acknowledged, with SASVA platform cited as a response.

qa_highlights.question: Has there been incremental due diligence on Nagarro's books given BaFin queries, and why is the multiple at a premium?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legal and tax diligence on BaFin queries (carve-out from Allgeier and accounting principles) found no impact on performance; the premium was described as reasonable for a control transaction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nagarro run independently for two years post-closing, and why no cash-plus-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent will work with management and aim for a squeeze-out over about 2 years, with no hurry. Management said a share swap was not feasible under German public-to-private dynamics; no QIP or dilution planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp and margin profile of the large deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is net new with little ramp needed, end-to-end product engineering and support, accretive from Q2, at a fairly healthy margin above company average.

qa_highlights.question: How will the combined entity sustain growth given Nagarro's slow growth and the long tail of accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to cross-selling of ERP/CX and mining of 180 $1M+ logos, with tail-account rationalisation possible to release SG&A. It said Nagarro's recent growth was affected by distraction from its take-private process.

qa_highlights.question: Decision tree on acceptance: what if below 50%, and what follows above 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistent holds 21% via SPA; management board commitment of about 13-14% takes it near 35%, with another 35-40% considered broadly committed. Management sees 50%+ as very likely; majority gives control of the supervisory board.

risks_watch: Regulatory approvals (including RBI and various EU jurisdictions) and BaFin clearance of the offer document; close targeted Q4 CY26 to early Q1 CY27.
Acceptance level versus the 50%+1 minimum; leverage moves between 1.9x and 2.5x depending on acceptance.
Nagarro's revenue flat for about two years, with several vertical declines (horizontal tech, energy/utilities, telecom, travel) flagged by analysts.
Integration of a two-year squeeze-out path with minority shareholders; synergy plan and value-creation plan not yet shared.
Cash conversion and debt servicing of roughly €1.4bn of acquisition debt, plus the T&M model and AI cannibalisation risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on strategic fit, growth and margin ambitions, but deliberately evasive on specifics pending regulatory approvals (no synergy numbers, value-creation plan, or customer names). Pushback was given to analysts on Nagarro's EBIT margins and the premium paid.
key_quotes: This is not a consolidation play. This is an expansion play for us bringing together, as Anand rightly pointed out, people, capabilities, markets which are all complimentary to us
we believe we have paid a reasonable premium for a control transaction.
we do not believe that the combined entity will be at any significant lower margins than what Persistent has today.
We don't intend doing any QIP, just to be clear for everyone. We don't intend diluting our stake at this point in time.

growth.why: Management flagged a net-new ~$125M annual (~$650M over 6.5 years) deal with an existing US customer, accretive from Q2, plus the debt-funded Nagarro acquisition (EV €1.27bn), but gave no organic revenue guidance and no Q1 FY27 results were discussed.
